Compensating the deterministic envelope in (5.4) gives E d_t <= beta_0(t)+(5/4)int_0^t b(u)omega(t-u)du +sum_{tau_j<t} omega(t-tau_j). (5.5) The same calculation applies to the pre-event states at deterministic slots. All future-dependent propagators were bounded BEFORE compensation. No anticipative stochastic-integral kernel has been treated as predictable. For continuous channels, the sum of absolute conditional rate errors equals b(t) max_{z_e in{+1,-1}} Tr[(eta-sigma_s)sum z_e R_e/b(t)] and is at most b(t)d_t. For a slot, categorical mark-law TV is one half the corresponding signed-effect maximum, so it is at most d_t/2. This accounts for the different target weights in dA. Up to that point their full register paths, permitted records, controls and reference banks agree. Thereafter preserve each law's proper marginal. The failure probability is at most the expected sum/integral of stopped mismatch risks. Drop the stop indicator only in this nonnegative bound under the unchanged actual marginal, insert (5.5), and obtain (4.2). This proves the record theorem under every admitted common causal policy. Finding the small invariant module, its kinetic coefficients, its feasible moment body, and these conditional preparation data may still be difficult. An abstract dimension count does not acquire them. The spin Bloch balls and fermion covariance bodies in the companion constructions are explicit cases. The exact filter can require a much larger space because measurement superoperators send V into products or other new observables. The theorem does not assert exact filter closure. It bounds the effect of ignoring this growth by the actual chronological access to those newly created directions. Operational equivalence corollary. Two microscopic models have the same implemented reduced law when they share: register labels and prior; ALL reference-bank initializations, including initially unoccupied modes; restricted fast coefficient functions and rate/pulse effect coefficients in V; channel and slot target maps, reported/coarse labels and slot schedule; and the entire initialized causal policy and its independent coin law. Occupied-mode bank moments match the corresponding physical conditional preparation moments in each model. Equal rate effects alone are insufficient: hidden target maps determine which persistent states become occupied. Their permitted-record TV is at most the sum of their two certified errors. Their initial correlations and post-event CP outputs need not agree. Even the microscopic dimensions may differ if the same positive moment representation and effect coefficients are realized in both. This follows by triangle inequality, with each physical model meeting its own relaxation/access certificate. It does not identify unknown kinetic coefficients or prove that unmodeled persistent registers are absent. Within this contract the full post-event density transformation need not be acquired to calculate the reduced rates; its positivity, target mode and effect must still be warranted. 8. LOCALIZATION, NUMERICS AND INITIAL MODE DATA If implementable bank coordinates give, on the SAME record, a uniform error zeta(t) for every normalized signed rate/slot effect, an additional allowance is int zeta(t)dA(t), by a second minimum-rate/maximal-mark coupling. The algorithm must be causal with valid intensities and slot probabilities. This bank-effect certificate does not automatically cover numerical belief-filter, event-sampler or controller error; those must be absent or separately bounded by conditional kernel errors. Coordinate accuracy also needs the dual effect norm. An expected certificate must specify its correct comparison marginal. Errors under an unrelated record distribution do not suffice. The fermionic companion derives zeta from a spatial cut and a supplied local conditional covariance block. It uses the unknown full initial covariance only in the proof, never as an implementation oracle. Generic full-density banks still need their full conditional priors or an explicit initial bound. An error in p_s can be charged separately by its probability TV when the entire initialized causal policy and all bank initialization are held fixed; compare the initial register mixture through its common future record kernel. In particular the controller's supplied prior input is held fixed in this comparison. Changing that input or its filter/controller computations may change the future kernel and needs a separate allowance. Computational costs include all matrix actions, mode/channel evaluation, fast-flow integration, precision, actual control bandwidth and preparation acquisition. Exact Gaussian or symmetry-reduced filters are stronger incumbents where their assumptions hold. A microscopic window simulator stores a sampled configuration rather than its entire distribution, but processes fast events; neither baseline can be dismissed from coordinate count alone. The record contract excludes unreported fast bath emissions, arbitrary final quantum-state recovery, and external-reference/diamond-norm guarantees. If the detector observes fast bath channels, their rate/effects must enter b and V. Critical rescalings or unrestricted control maps likewise require rechecking the effect norm, module and access certificate. No physical covariance-action oracle is assumed by the mathematical covariance coordinate representation. 9. WHAT THE CURRENT STATE PREDICTS AFTER AN OBSERVED PAST Let the complete permitted record on [0,T] split at a deterministic time t as (H,F), including known controller inputs when needed. These are standard Borel spaces. If the theorem gives TV(P_(H,F),Pbar_(H,F))<=epsilon, then E_(H~P_H) TV(P(F in . |H),Pbar(F in . |H))<=2epsilon. (9.1) This is an average conditional prediction guarantee under the ACTUAL past law. It is not a uniformly accurate posterior on every rare history. Proof. Choose regular conditional future kernels K_P,K_bar and define R(dh,df)=P_H(dh) K_bar(h,df). Then TV(P,R)=int TV(K_P(h,.),K_bar(h,.))P_H(dh), TV(Pbar,R)=TV(Pbar_H,P_H). Triangle inequality and marginal contraction prove (9.1). An arbitrary measurable extension on Pbar_H-null histories also satisfies this bound. For an implemented current-state law choose a state-based extension there. Its future kernel depends on time, the current banks and mode belief, and ALL current controller/coefficient-evaluation state. It need not retain the past separately when that state already contains the controller's sufficient memory; a controller that itself stores its whole history still pays for it. A past of probability epsilon may have completely wrong conditional futures while total record TV is only epsilon. No rare-history certification follows without additional assumptions or a separate conditional bound. STATUS AND SOURCES OF THE SCOPED CHECKS The argument is a first-principles finite-dimensional construction. Exact root draft ffca999f8fc54a985888ac7956605b91f8d528204e0895b9bc00f0ab00c18794 was checked independently in this producing thread: Sections 1-6 by agents/conditional_memory_construction_20261024/ ROOT_QUANTUM_PARTIAL_MEMORY_SECTIONS_1_6_AUDIT.txt, and Sections 7-8 by agents/predictive_state_obstruction_20261024/ QUANTUM_MOMENT_MODULE_SCOPED_AUDIT_ffca999f8fc5.txt. Section 9 has its separate short proof in AVERAGE_CONDITIONAL_RECORD_PREDICTION_LEMMA.txt in the latter directory. This version incorporates the exact shared-interface, null-slot and numerical/controller qualifications identified in those checks. The spin and fermion corollaries provide explicit positive economical modules. The transient-capture construction and primary predecessor notes are preserved separately. These are complementary native proof checks, not external independent validation. Existing Green, critical-spin and local-law sources remain unchanged. Historical novelty, acquired physical access and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.

5. PROOF: LAST-EVENT RESTART, NONCOMMUTING NO-EVENT DRIFT, COUPLING

Condition in the proof on the complete slow-event history, the initial
register label, and slot outcomes. Between these events, s is fixed and
the normalized fast conditional state solves
  eta'=A_s eta -{R^s,eta}/2+Tr(R^s eta)eta.                (5.1)
This equation includes the effect of observing NO event. Replacing it by
the unconditional covariance/mean equation would miss measurement memory.

For a terminal effect F and an interval with no event, variation of constants
for eta-sigma_s propagates its initial difference through U^s and integrates
the forcing in (5.1). Pairing that forcing with G=U^{s,*}_{u,t}F gives
  -Cov_sym,eta(R^s,G)
  =-Re Tr[eta(R^s-Tr eta R^s)(G-Tr eta G)].                (5.2)
The state-weighted Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the spectral variance bound
Var_eta(X)<=osc(X)^2/4 imply
  |Cov_sym,eta(R^s,G)|<=b(u)omega(t-u)/4.                 (5.3)
No commutativity of eta, R or G is used.

Restart at the MOST RECENT slow event or slot before the target time. Its
post-event eta and the current target-mode bank are both density matrices.
Their trace distance is <=1, so the propagated mismatch is <=omega of the
elapsed time. If no event occurred, use beta_0(t) instead. Taking positive
upper bounds permits replacing the last event by a sum over all earlier
events and extending the no-event integral to [0,t]. Pathwise, uniformly in
the terminal effect,
  d_t <= beta_0(t)
      +sum_{continuous events u<t} omega(t-u)
      +sum_{tau_j<t} omega(t-tau_j)
      +(1/4)int_0^t b(u)omega(t-u)du.                    (5.4)
This d_t bounds the relevant effect difference, not full trace distance.

At a deterministic target t, the total continuous event intensity is <=b.
Compensating the deterministic envelope in (5.4) gives
  E d_t <= beta_0(t)+(5/4)int_0^t b(u)omega(t-u)du
                        +sum_{tau_j<t} omega(t-tau_j).  (5.5)
The same calculation applies to the pre-event states at deterministic slots.
All future-dependent propagators were bounded BEFORE compensation. No
anticipative stochastic-integral kernel has been treated as predictable.

For continuous channels, the sum of absolute conditional rate errors equals
  b(t) max_{z_e in{+1,-1}} Tr[(eta-sigma_s)sum z_e R_e/b(t)]
and is at most b(t)d_t. For a slot, categorical mark-law TV is one half the
corresponding signed-effect maximum, so it is at most d_t/2. This accounts
for the different target weights in dA. A slot's own post-event disturbance
is relevant only to LATER targets, hence the strict order s<t and no
same-slot diagonal term in (4.2).

Couple the continuous marked processes at minimum rates and the slot marks
maximally, until their first unmatched event. Up to that point their full
register paths, permitted records, controls and reference banks agree.
Thereafter preserve each law's proper marginal. The failure probability is
at most the expected sum/integral of stopped mismatch risks. Drop the stop
indicator only in this nonnegative bound under the unchanged actual marginal,

admitted common causal policy.                                             QED

6. WHY ARBITRARY FEEDBACK-SELECTED PULSE TIMES REQUIRE MORE

Instrument CHOICES at the deterministic slots can be arbitrary causal
functions of Y. A deterministic grid of potential slots also dominates an
adaptively chosen subset. The proof does not automatically extend to arbitrary
record-selected continuous pulse times by substituting those random times in

created discrepancy. The weight omega(tau-s) then depends on a future event
and cannot be compensated as if deterministic. A new conditional timing
certificate or a direct pathwise exposure bound is required.

This is a substantive information-access issue. A finite number of fast
interventions can convert a short transient into persistent register memory.
The independent two-bit construction preserves a later record gap with two
O(gamma)-rate, O(1/gamma)-duration pulses and bounded integrated control
hazard. It is not a contradiction of (4.2): its ordered exposure does not
vanish. Exact supplied action maps can sometimes transport a retained state
and repair the approximation; that interface must be derived, not assumed.

7. SMALL OBSERVABLE MODULE INSTEAD OF THE FULL REFERENCE DENSITY

Let V be a real self-adjoint linear space containing I, invariant under every
admitted fast adjoint A_s^*, and containing all continuous and slot effects.

I,v_1,...,v_d. The current bank coordinates are
  z_{s,l}=Tr(sigma_s v_l).

  C_V={(Tr(rho v_l))_l:rho>=0,Tr rho=1}

nonnegative on this body.

data are the slow prior and these conditional moments; full conditional

The current reference state has rd+r-1 real coordinates plus the controller.

Finding the small invariant module, its kinetic coefficients, its feasible
moment body, and these conditional preparation data may still be difficult.
An abstract dimension count does not acquire them. The spin Bloch balls and
fermion covariance bodies in the companion constructions are explicit cases.

superoperators send V into products or other new observables. The theorem
does not assert exact filter closure. It bounds the effect of ignoring this
growth by the actual chronological access to those newly created directions.

implemented reduced law when they share: register labels and prior; ALL
reference-bank initializations, including initially unoccupied modes;
restricted fast coefficient functions and rate/pulse effect coefficients in
V; channel and slot target maps, reported/coarse labels and slot schedule;
and the entire initialized causal policy and its independent coin law.

preparation moments in each model. Equal rate effects alone are insufficient:

initial correlations and post-event CP outputs need not agree. Even the
microscopic dimensions may differ if the same positive moment representation
and effect coefficients are realized in both. This follows by triangle
inequality, with each physical model meeting its own relaxation/access
certificate. It does not identify unknown kinetic coefficients or prove that
unmodeled persistent registers are absent. Within this contract the full
post-event density transformation need not be acquired to calculate the
reduced rates; its positivity, target mode and effect must still be warranted.

Borel spaces. If the theorem gives TV(P_(H,F),Pbar_(H,F))<=epsilon, then

memory; a controller that itself stores its whole history still pays for it.

while total record TV is only epsilon. No rare-history certification follows

not under every measurement superoperator, if the missing conditional
information is charged through a quantitative relaxation/access certificate.

driven reference states retains the response to known controls. This is an
approximate generative/record law, not an exact filter or a full quantum-state
approximation. Prior, kinetic, instrument and computational inputs remain real
obligations. No priority or experimental-capability claim is made.

1. HYBRID QUANTUM MODEL AND INFORMATION CONTRACT

Let s range over a finite classical register S of size r, and let the fast
sector have a finite-dimensional Hilbert space H. The physical state is
block diagonal in s; quantum coherences between register labels are outside
this model. Conditional fast states can be arbitrary, including entangled
many-body states. Initially S has probabilities p_s and conditional states
mu_s. For p_s=0 an arbitrary conditional state can be assigned.

For each s and permitted known history h, A_s(t,h) is a trace-preserving
Lindblad generator for the fast sector. Its coefficients and propagators are
well posed on the finite horizon. Fast coefficients may vary arbitrarily
rapidly with known controls. No stationary reference or slow-control
assumption is imposed. The actual coefficient maps are supplied/calibrated;
energy ratios alone do not identify them.

Slow channels e at mode s have completely positive maps J_e^s(t,h), target
mode tau(s,e), and effects
  R_e^s=J_e^{s,*}(I)>=0,  R^s=sum_e R_e^s<=b(t) I.             (1.1)
Here b is a deterministic nonnegative integrable envelope, uniform over all
admitted histories and modes. Finite channel lists suffice. Each channel
has a declared observed label or a hidden label. Channels can preserve or
change s and can reset or entangle the fast sector arbitrarily. The physical
rate in a conditional fast state eta is Tr(R_e^s eta), and the post-event
state is J_e^s(eta)/Tr(R_e^s eta) when this rate is positive. Zero-rate events
do not occur; their nominal post-state is immaterial.

The direct-sum master equation consists of A_s, the outgoing term
-{R^s,rho_s}/2, and the incoming CP maps from all channels. It is a valid
trace-preserving positive quantum evolution on the classical-quantum state
space. In particular a quadratic or affine rate effect does NOT determine
the CP output map; the latter is part of the supplied kinetic instrument.

Optionally supply deterministic slots
  0<tau_1<...<tau_J<=T.
At slot j a controlled instrument has CP maps K_{j,e}^s, target mode
tau_j(s,e), and effects
  E_{j,e}^s=K_{j,e}^{s,*}(I)>=0,  sum_e E_{j,e}^s=I.           (1.2)
Only the prescribed coarse outcome is reported. Instrument choices at the
slots can depend arbitrarily on the permitted past record. A slot whose every
outcome is hidden applies its all-outcome stochastic
operation to the register. If only some outcomes are reported, the known
null result uses its corresponding outcome subset. Simultaneous instruments
must be explicitly ordered and
their zero-lag cross terms charged; strict ordering above avoids ambiguity.

The controller sees only the declared coarsened record Y and independent
supplied coins. It cannot see s, hidden marks, bath emissions, or private
simulation variables. Every model executes the SAME causal policy on its
own Y. Any controller computations used to choose controls are part of that
same initialized program and remain charged. This includes its controller
initial data, supplied parameters and coin law; identical program text with
different initialization need not give the same causal policy. The full
register/slow-event record used
below is a proof device, not an extra measurement supplied to the controller.

2. DRIVEN BANKS AND THE CLOSED REDUCED REGISTER FILTER

known record retain one counterfactual bank per mode:

event or at a slot. Its generator can change through known feedback.

These define a genuine classical hidden-register model. It can be implemented
through its exact finite-state belief p_hat conditioned on Y, without storing

that change s (hidden self-events do not change this generator). For an
observed continuous mark a, form the nonnegative RATE matrix
  M_a(s,s')=sum_{e: target=s', observed=a} qbar_e^s.

  Q=Q_0+sum_a [M_a-diag(m_a)].

All divisions are used only on positive-probability marks. Thus observed
events can change the register and measurement can have fast back-action.

hidden elementary marks with observed outcome a and the indicated target.

this update would be wrong when the intervention changes the register.

Computational costs include all matrix actions, mode/channel evaluation,

The record contract excludes unreported fast bath emissions, arbitrary final

9. WHAT THE CURRENT STATE PREDICTS AFTER AN OBSERVED PAST

Let the complete permitted record on [0,T] split at a deterministic time t
as (H,F), including known controller inputs when needed. These are standard
Borel spaces. If the theorem gives TV(P_(H,F),Pbar_(H,F))<=epsilon, then
  E_(H~P_H) TV(P(F in . |H),Pbar(F in . |H))<=2epsilon.     (9.1)
This is an average conditional prediction guarantee under the ACTUAL past
law. It is not a uniformly accurate posterior on every rare history.

Proof. Choose regular conditional future kernels K_P,K_bar and define
R(dh,df)=P_H(dh) K_bar(h,df). Then
  TV(P,R)=int TV(K_P(h,.),K_bar(h,.))P_H(dh),
  TV(Pbar,R)=TV(Pbar_H,P_H).
Triangle inequality and marginal contraction prove (9.1). An arbitrary
measurable extension on Pbar_H-null histories also satisfies this bound.
For an implemented current-state law choose a state-based extension there.
Its future kernel depends on time, the current banks and mode belief, and
ALL current controller/coefficient-evaluation state. It need not retain the
past separately when that state already contains the controller's sufficient
memory; a controller that itself stores its whole history still pays for it.

A past of probability epsilon may have completely wrong conditional futures
while total record TV is only epsilon. No rare-history certification follows
without additional assumptions or a separate conditional bound.
